title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page (numbered '- 18 -'), photographed upside down. Its content has nothing to do with the handwritten motivic and Brandt-groupoid notes on the neighbouring pages. It is almost certainly a sheet of someone else's typescript, reused by Grothendieck as scrap paper. It gives the standard proof of the analytic implicit function theorem over a complete valued field K, in the Bourbaki style ('séries entières sommables dans un polycylindre').

Statement being proved: let f_1,...,f_q(x;y) be analytic near (a,b) with f_i(a,b)=0 and the Jacobian det(∂f_i/∂y_j)(a,b) ≠ 0. Then there is a unique analytic solution y=u(x) near a with u(a)=b. The page opens on the end of the uniqueness statement: any analytic v with f(x,v(x))=0 near a coincides with u.

Proof as given:
1. Translate so that a=0 and b=0.
2. Expand each f_i in y as f_i = f_{i0}(x) + Σ_j f_{ij}(x) y_j + (terms of total degree ≥2 in y). The coefficients are power series in x convergent on a polycylinder P, and f_{i0}(0)=0.
3. The matrix F=(f_{ij}(x)) is invertible at 0, hence on a smaller polycylinder P_1, with holomorphic inverse G=(g_{ij}).
4. Replace f by g = G·f. Then g_i = -h_{i0} + y_i - Σ h_{i;n} y^n, so the linear part in y is exactly the identity.
5. The existence part is thereby reduced to solving the fixed-point system u_i = h_{i0} + Σ h_{i;n} u^n with u(0)=0, by power series in x convergent near 0.

The argument presumably continues on the next typed page with formal recursive solution plus Cauchy majorant series.
errors: No mathematical errors. The reduction is correct: since G·F = I identically in x, the y-linear part of g_i is exactly y_i, and the constant term -h_{i0} = Σ g_{ij} f_{j0} has no constant term.
The typescript itself has a typographical slip, 'tra-nslation'.

ideas.what: Analytic implicit function theorem over a complete valued field, proved by normalising the linear part with the inverse Jacobian matrix and solving the resulting fixed-point system of power series
ideas.modern_name: Implicit function theorem for analytic functions over complete valued fields (method of majorants / Cauchy–Kovalevskaya-type argument)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (majorant method); the non-archimedean and general-field presentation is standard (e.g. Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques; Serre, Lie Algebras and Lie Groups, Part II)
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material (Bourbaki VAR, Serre LALG); not a Grothendieck text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine typescript page, apparently not by Grothendieck, reused as scrap paper. It contains a textbook proof of the analytic implicit function theorem and has no connection to the surrounding motivic/Galois notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is physically upside down; the content is a typescript, not handwriting, and is unrelated to the handwritten notes on the neighbouring pages.
'tra-nslation' is a typo in the original typescript, not a transcription error.
